alyssa (devex): Quick report: the generator example in quickstart causes hung tests if the process receives SIGTERM during a long stream. reproducer in sandbox shows goroutines stuck waiting on io.Read.

lee (infra): seen that in e2e too. containers don't shut down cleanly because the sample uses context.Background() and never wires signal handling.

tom (go-sdk): thanks. i want to avoid surprising app behavior. our current doc shows the minimalist loop which is cute for examples but unsafe for production. two related issues: (1) ownership of cancel semantics is unclear, (2) network reconnects (auth refresh) can leave iterator blocked.

alyssa (devex): users copy the example verbatim into templates. can we provide a drop-in helper so folks have correct signal + timeout behavior by default?

tom (go-sdk): proposal: add a NewGenerator function that takes options. by default it will wrap an incoming context if it's non-cancellable (like Background) with an internal cancel linked to Close(). option WithExternalCtxPreserved bool would opt out. better: provide NewGeneratorAutoCancel(ctx, req) which returns (it, cancel) so samples are explicit but short.

lee (infra): that sounds good. also for auth-reconnect: i recommend the iterator surface error states instead of blocking. e.g. Err() returns errors.Is(err, ErrAuthReconnect) so callers know to retry the whole operation.

tom (go-sdk): agreed. implementation notes: replace long-blocking read with select { case <-done: return; case tok := <-tokCh: ... } and ensure Close() signals done. also ensure that any reconnect path writes an error into an errCh that causes Next() to return false.

alyssa (devex): could we also show a tiny pattern in onboarding that wires up signal.NotifyContext and a context timeout around the generator? Helps new devs see the right way. sample snippet something like:```go
ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt)
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second)
defer cancel()
it, finish := client.NewGeneratorAutoCancel(ctx, req)
defer finish()
for it.Next() { fmt.Print(it.Token()) }
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("stream failed: %v", err) }
```

tom (go-sdk): nice. small API detail: finish() should call it.Close() under the hood and be idempotent. i also want to add a convenience method it.TryNext(ctx) that accepts a per-Next deadline so callers can avoid a global timeout for the whole stream. that might be controversial though.

lee (infra): TryNext sounds useful for interactive apps, but keep the core simple for onboarding. add TryNext in an advanced section.

alyssa (devex): docs-wise: add a 'Common gotchas' bullet in quickstart: "don't use context.Background() without cancellation for long-lived streams" and link to the helper. i'll draft the paragraph and the sample patch.

tom (go-sdk): engineering plan: (1) add NewGeneratorAutoCancel helper + finish() semantics, (2) wiring Close() to cancel/internal done chan, (3) make Next() return false on reconnect with Err set, (4) add unit + e2e that simulates mid-stream auth refresh and SIGTERM. i'll open a draft PR and tag you for review. ETA 3 business days.

alyssa (devex): tiny UX note: in the sample snippet let's prefer signal.NotifyContext so examples are small and idiomatic. also show an example comment about when to prefer WithTimeout vs per-Next timeout.

tom (go-sdk): will do. i'll include a short note in the changelog: "go sdk: generator helper + safer cancellation semantics; iterator now surfaces reconnect errors instead of blocking". also add migration note: callers relying on blocking behavior should switch to NewGeneratorAutoCancel or call Close() explicitly.
